newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS NEWS - AUGUST 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS NEWS - AUGUST 7.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- TUBE WORKERS IN 1,000 STG BONANZA

In an bid to avoid further delays in the 2.6bn stg Jubilee Line extension of the London Underground, contractors are offering their staff up to 1,000 stg in bonuses and overtime payments. London Underground has denied the timetable for the project is slipping and that it could be delayed until the end of the decade, though contractors claim they are under much pressure and 'cannot allow the project to get behind' and as a result have had to work longer hours and recruit more staff.
-- HAYS WINS PETROL WAR DEAL

Logistics group Hays has secured a five-year 100m stg contract to distribute goods to BP shops and is now looking to gain business from oil companies battling supermarkets who poach their petrol sales. The BP contract will create 500 jobs and will cut out wholesaler Palmer & Harvey as well as many direct suppliers and will save BP 15m stg and according to a BP spokesman will bring more consistency to the range and quality of goods sold in BP shops.
-- SAATCHI PAYS OFF PREGNANT DIRECTOR AT MEGALOMEDIA

Lord Saatchi, head of new media empire Megalomedia, has given a director at the company a 30,000 stg pay-off after she became pregnant. The woman had offered to remain at the company and work a three-day week, but the company declared that would be inappropriate as it was 'pushing business very hard'. A spokesperson for Megalomedia stated the agreement was 'amicable'. The woman will also be permitted to exercise her options on her 240,000 shares, which are valued at 179,000 stg.
THE TIMES
-- WICKES SUES CHIEFS TO RECOVER BONUSES

DIY retailer Wickes is suing two of its former bosses, Les Rosenthal and Chris Miles, in an attempt to recover 136,000 stg in bonus payments. Miles and Rosenthal were suspended, and later resigned from the company last June, when a 51m stg hole was found in its accounts. The Serious Fraud Office opened investigations into the company's problems last November, and while no charges have been made, the investigation are continuing.
-- CHRYSALIS BUYS RADIO STATION FOR 17.6M STG

Chrysalis has acquired Yorkshire's Kiss FM in a 17.6m stg deal which makes it the largest UK radio broadcaster after the BBC, as it already owns the London and Manchester Heart radio stations. Chrysalis' radio division head, Richard Huntingford, said the company will now compare Kiss with its own Cardiff-based Galaxy station in an attempt to determine which is more popular and will be given country-wide broadcast and which will be scrapped.
-- MALL OPERATOR PUTS VALUATION AT 1.75BN STG

Central Shopping Centres, which owns and operates eight UK malls including Lakeside and the MetroCentre, has increased its revaluation surplus by 135m stg, to 1.75bn stg. The revaluation serves as further proof of the increasing strength in the retail property market, and CSC declared from now it would have its net asset value reassessed twice per year. CSC also reported a 31 per cent leap in its interim pre-tax profits, to 36.3m stg.
THE GUARDIAN
-- GEC CHIEF GETS 1M STG WELCOME

Electronics group GEC revealed on Wednesday in its annual report that new chief executive George Simpson received over 1m stg for his six months at the company, including a 500,000 stg signing bonus. The report also revealed a controversial new share option scheme and announced former trade minister Sir Richard Needham would be leaving the company at the end of September to join NEC.
-- CADBURY ADOPTS SMARTIE APPROACH

Food and drink group Cadbury Schweppes has launched a new confectionery product named Astros which are imported from South Africa, similar to Smarties, and whose launch will be backed by a 6m stg advertising campaign. Cadbury also reported half year profits of 653m stg and a ten per cent rise in underlying profits, both of which were boosted by the sale of its UK bottling operation to Coca-Cola.
-- MICHELS TIPPED FOR GRANADA

Stakis chief executive David Michels has emerged as the favoured candidate to head up Granada's hotels division following the resignation of Patrick Copeland earlier in the year. Granada, Britain's largest hotelier, has appointed a team of headhunters to search out possible candidates and while Michels has not yet been approached, he is understood to be the front runner.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- TELEWEST PREPARES TO SLASH 1,400 JOBS IN BID TO CUT COSTS

Telewest Communications, the second largest British cable group, will reportedly announce on Thursday cuts of up to 1,400 jobs as part of a new cost-cutting review which will also include spending curbs. Shares in Telewest have experienced a continual decline over the past few months, due to concern over costs from its huge investment programme. The company has been reluctance to elaborate on its merger with NTL and on Thursday afternoon will unveil its interim results.
-- POON TIES KNOT WITH BROOKS

Hong Kong multi-millionaire Dickson Poon, credited with rejuvenating the Harvey Nichols stores group and owner of such brands as Polo, Rolex, Hermes and Bulgari, has signed an exclusive 10-year franchise contract with Marks & Spencer offshoot Brooks. Poon's Dickson Concepts International will begin selling Brooks products in Hong Kong and Southern Asian outlets next year. Poon also revealed new agreements with a number of groups, including Ferrari and Inter Perfumes.
-- PETERS RESIGNS FROM ONE 2 ONE TO RETURN TO THE US

Jan Peters has resigned as managing director of UK mobile network One 2 One to run MediaOne, the cable group owned by US West, a joint shareholder of One 2 One. While much of the industry was stunned by Peters' departure, One 2 One stressed it was a promotion which she simply could not turn down. Peters had been credited with initiating a major turnaround at the mobile group, increasing its number of customers from 410,000 to over 700,000 in her year at the company.
